To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
changes of FC, NLs, and MAP2 immunoreactivities are different temporally, spatially, and cell types between the core and the penumbra in rat brain after 90 min MCAO.

the loss of FC and the accumulation of NLs in the core and the accumulation of both in the penumbara were associated with the degenerative and the regenerative neural processes, respectively, after transient MCAo.
the changes of FC and NLS are different temporally in relation to degeneration and regeneration in the ischemic brain.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the effects of transient middle cerebral occlusion on the lipid metabolism in rat brain.
the role of cholesterol and neutral lipoproteins in the pathogenesis of ischemic brain injury and in the recovery of function after ischemia.
the temporal and spatial changes in free cholesterol (FC), and neutral lipid droplets (NLs), after a transient middle cerebral artery (MCA) occlusion.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
FC and NLs in brain tissue change in a complex manner after transient brain ischemia.

the changes of FC and neutral lipids are different temporally between the ischemic core and penumbral region, and that the loss of FC is closely related to the degeneration of neurons and the increase in NL is related to the regenerative process of astrocytes in the ischemic penumbra.

the results of the present study indicate that the temporal and spatial changes in free cholesterol and neutral lipid droplets in the brain following transient MCAO are closely related to the neural degenerative process and regenerative processes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the FC and NLs were decreased in the core and increased in the periphery during the first week, which may be related with degenerative process.
the changes of lipid metabolism in relation with degenerative neural process in the ischemic region are different from those in the penumbral area where the regenerative process is observed.

lipid droplets are produced and accumulated in microglia in the ischemic lesion core and in astrocytes in the penumbral area during the first week after ischemic insult, and that the lipid droplets in microglia are degraded and the lipid droplets within astrocytes are increased during the second to third week.
The main takeaway from our work is that
changes of FC are related to neural degeneration in the core, whereas those of NLs are related to neural regeneration in the penumbura.
there are different temporal and spatial changes in free cholesterol and neutral lipid levels in the ischemic brain.
the changes of FC and NLS are different temporally in the penumbral area.
